rows.why: Item 2 asks how loosely a stored value is cleaned before it is matched. S1 depends on that answer: case and padding must be ignored. The pick trims and lowercases, so "Draft", " PUBLISHED " and "Merged" read as draft, published and merged.

Item 1 asks which old spellings map to a status. S2 expects a table of eleven, including under review, live, assigned and done. The pick maps only "in review", so "under_review" and "LIVE" would read as null instead of review and published.

Item 3 asks what an unrecognised or empty stored value reads as. The pick returns null for those, and for whitespace-only values, without guessing the nearest status. That matches S3, which expects no status at all.
S4 only checks that a canonical status is stored unchanged. No item asks about that. Item 4 covers non-canonical input, and how it is answered doesn't change what S4 expects.

Item 4 asks whether writing accepts non-canonical input such as other case, padding or old spellings. S5 says it must not. The pick requires an exact canonical match, so "Review", "in-review" and " draft" throw. The error message from item 5 includes the value, which also fits S5.

Item 8 asks how unreadable values are reported from a batch read. S6 wants each distinct original value listed once, sorted, exactly as stored. The pick reports the raw strings unmodified, removes duplicates and sorts them. Item 7 only covers part of S6, which is why item 8 is the closer match.
